Rafael / Aditya —

Thanks for the context. Draft proposal below (high level) and attached an "evidence package" template (evidence-package-template.pdf). I tried to keep the carve-out narrow and operationally feasible:

1) Contract language (suggested insertion to Section 9.3 — Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, damages arising from a confirmed Confidentiality Breach that results in the misappropriation or unauthorized disclosure of Customer's trade secrets shall not be subject to the monetary cap set forth in this Agreement, provided that the Customer provides (i) written notice within 30 days of discovery, (ii) a forensics report prepared by an independent third-party forensic investigator reasonably acceptable to Redwood, and (iii) evidence of chain-of-custody for the impacted materials. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to limit any award to documented, direct damages attributable to the breach."

2) Evidence package (attached): recommended components Redwood will accept as triggering evidence:
- Incident timeline with UTC timestamps and affected resource IDs
- Forensic report summary + investigator contact
- Hash values or samples demonstrating the specific data classified as trade secret
- Chain-of-custody forms and access logs
- Signed certification from Customer's CISO asserting trade-secret status (template included)

3) Signature / storage flow:
- Carve-out acknowledgement: executed as an addendum to the MSA; DocuSign acceptable.
- Evidence attachments: collected by Customer and uploaded to the shared drive link (encrypted folder) with SHA256 checksums; Redwood SRE/Trust will attach an authenticated message receipt.
- Retention: Redwood will retain the audit trail and the DocuSign record for at least 7 years (or as required under law).

4) Monetary cap options (for negotiation):
- Option A: unlimited for proven trade-secret exfiltration (likely a hard sell)
- Option B: fixed carve-out cap per incident: $5,000,000
- Option C: tiered approach tied to ARR band (we can flesh this with Sales)

Notes / open items for Legal Ops: who signs the forensic acceptance (Redwood's Trust lead or Redwood General Counsel), and whether we want a timebox for presenting forensics (e.g., 90 days after discovery).

If this direction looks OK, I can turn it into redline language for their doc and include an evidence-package checklist Cryptoware can fill out.

-Monica
Monica Patel
